title: PerovAgent: Autonomous Ligand Design for Halide Perovskite Nanocrystals
authors: Seungjun Cha, Yoo Jae Jeong, Amanda Conde Del Moral, Juan-Pablo Correa-Baena, Seth R. Marder, David S. Ginger
abstract: Designing surface-capping ligands for high-performance halide perovskite nanocrystals requires navigating a vast molecular space while discovering design rules that govern ligand-surface interactions. Here, we introduce PerovAgent, an autonomous multi-agent framework that combines large language model (LLM)-driven scientific reasoning with computational tools for atomistic model construction, machine-learned interatomic potential evaluation, and statistical validation. Across ten independent campaigns on CsPbBr3 surfaces, PerovAgent adaptively explored and refined diverse ligand chemistries while progressively improving the binding-energy objective. Beyond optimization, the framework converts recurring chemical observations into explicit design principles that can be statistically evaluated. Of 35 formulated principles, 19 were prospectively supported, of which seven also passed the confound audit, highlighting the need to systematically validate plausible LLM-generated hypotheses during autonomous discovery. A recurrent alkynyl-phosphonate principle was further examined using density functional theory, which reproduced the predicted energetic preference. These results demonstrate an autonomous discovery framework that not only searches molecular space and optimizes the scalar objective but also transforms its search trajectory into systematically testable design principles. The framework can also be extended to more complex ligands, including zwitterionic, multidentate, and polymerizable ligands, to explore a wider range of ligand-surface interactions and uncover new design principles for halide perovskite nanocrystals.

infographic.key_insight: PerovAgent autonomously designs ligands for halide perovskite nanocrystals while turning search observations into statistically testable chemical design principles.
infographic.engineering_relevance: The framework could guide surface-ligand engineering for perovskite materials, though solar-cell performance gains are not demonstrated in the abstract.
method: Combine LLM-driven multi-agent reasoning with atomistic model construction and machine-learned interatomic potentials.
Adaptively search ligand chemistries to improve binding energies on CsPbBr3 surfaces.
Validate proposed design principles statistically and examine a recurring alkynyl-phosphonate preference using density functional theory.
infographic.evidence_signal: Across 10 independent campaigns, 19 of 35 proposed principles received prospective support, seven also passed a confound audit, and DFT reproduced the alkynyl-phosphonate energetic preference.
infographic.watch_item: Limited survival through confound auditing underscores the need to validate LLM-generated hypotheses before using them as general design rules.
infographic.paper_title: PerovAgent: Autonomous Ligand Design for Halide Perovskite Nanocrystals

title: Evidence-grounded large language models guide perovskite solar cell design and optimization
authors: YanKai Chen, Zhi Wan, ZiHao Li, Tao Jing
abstract: Using large language models to interpret experimental evidence, design discriminating experiments and formulate well-supported mechanistic explanations remains a central challenge in materials research. Here we establish PSM-Bench, an 800-question benchmark developed by perovskite researchers to evaluate scientific reasoning in perovskite photovoltaics. We also introduce OpenPerov, an expert-informed language-model framework that learns from expert-calibrated evidence records reconstructed from 4,035 training articles; these records link experimental strategies, controls and observations to mechanistic interpretations. Structured-evidence adaptation outperformed conventional question-answer training, and OpenPerov Flash ranked first among 13 closed-book systems. OpenPerov Pro raised Scientific Mastery further, from 87.6 to 89.1, by revising selected passages with retrieved evidence. On questions derived from subsequent studies, both models also outscored expert-authored answers. In an experimental test of self-assembled monolayer design, OpenPerov selected a K analogue that outperformed the Na analogue preferred by experts. Devices incorporating the selected contact reached a power conversion efficiency of 27.05% and retained 96.74% of their initial efficiency after 1,000 h of dark thermal ageing at 85 $^\circ$C. These results show that reconstructed scientific reasoning provides an effective basis for building domain models that interpret experiments and inform materials design.

infographic.key_insight: Training language models on structured experimental evidence enabled OpenPerov to guide perovskite solar-cell design, selecting a contact that delivered 27.05% power conversion efficiency.
infographic.engineering_relevance: Evidence-grounded AI could help engineers select materials and design discriminating experiments for more efficient, thermally stable solar cells.
method: Reconstruct expert-calibrated evidence records from 4,035 training articles.
Adapt models using links between experimental strategies, controls, observations and mechanisms.
Refine selected answers with retrieved evidence and experimentally test a proposed contact.
infographic.evidence_signal: On the 800-question PSM-Bench, OpenPerov Flash ranked first among 13 closed-book systems; the selected contact yielded devices retaining 96.74% efficiency after 1,000 hours of dark thermal ageing at 85°C.
infographic.watch_item: The reported dark thermal-ageing result does not establish durability under illumination or outdoor operating conditions.
infographic.paper_title: Evidence-grounded large language models guide perovskite solar cell design and optimization

title: Enrichment-Oriented Virtual Screening of Perovskite Solar Cells through Reinforcement Learning
authors: Yezeyuan Zheng, Ziyang Hu, Maojun Sun, Ruijian Han, Jian Huang, Guanhua Chen
abstract: Experimental optimization of perovskite solar cells is constrained by combinatorial diversity in absorber compositions, device layers, and processing, which makes virtual screening attractive for prioritizing recipes before fabrication. We develop a surrogate-guided reinforcement-learning framework that casts recipe generation as virtual screening, enriching candidate shortlists near high-performing experimental neighbors. A frozen Tabular Prior-data Fitted Network (TabPFN) guides recipe generation, while a reference pool of 890 measured devices enables neighborhood-based assessment. Five-fold evaluation on 1,846 devices shows top-ten selection raises mean power conversion efficiency (PCE) from 19.68\% to 23.74\%. Three learned policies are compared with six baselines under 3,000 surrogate evaluations per run. In top-100 shortlists, Proximal policy optimization (PPO) and recurrent PPO (RPPO) achieve neighborhood-supported hit rates of 23\% and 24\% (7.9- and 8.3-fold Pure Random's 2.9\%), versus 10\% (3.4-fold) for the baselines with the highest supported hit rate (L-SHADE and Ax BO, tied) at $K = 100$. Gains coexist with weak-support fractions. Of 9,000 recipes, 65.4\% match a composition family at similarity 0.80, falling to 11.7\% at 0.90. Results support enrichment-oriented prioritization but not experimental performance, seed robustness, or matched-budget advantage.

infographic.key_insight: Surrogate-guided reinforcement learning enriched virtual perovskite recipe shortlists near high-performing measured devices, without demonstrating experimental performance gains.
infographic.engineering_relevance: The framework could help prioritize perovskite solar-cell recipes before costly fabrication and testing.
method: Generate candidate recipes with reinforcement-learning policies guided by a frozen TabPFN surrogate.
Assess neighborhood support using a reference pool of 890 measured devices.
Compare three learned policies with six baselines using 3,000 surrogate evaluations per run.
infographic.evidence_signal: Five-fold evaluation on 1,846 devices raised mean PCE from 19.68% to 23.74% through top-ten selection; top-100 neighborhood-supported hit rates reached 23–24% for PPO/RPPO versus 2.9% for Pure Random and 10% for the strongest baselines.
infographic.watch_item: Many generated recipes had weak experimental-neighborhood support, and experimental performance, seed robustness, and matched-budget advantage remain unestablished.

title: Hierarchical interfacial anchoring for durable perovskite solar cells
authors: Jiaxin Wu, Hongzhuo Wu, Zuhong Zhang, Xiaoyu Guan, Jinbo Zhao, Yuting Guo
abstract: Although inverted perovskite solar cells now deliver certified efficiencies approaching their single-junction limits, their practical deployment remains constrained by the thermo-mechanical fragility of buried interfaces under realistic temperature fluctuations. Here, we identify thermo-mechanically driven, stress-accumulation-dominated adhesion failure at self-assembled monolayer-based buried interfaces as a critical failure mode in inverted perovskite solar cells. To address this issue, we propose an interfacial robustness design strategy based on a homometallic halide pretreatment, which constructs a chemically compatible and highly anchorable interfacial environment on transparent conductive oxides to guide the ordered assembly of SAMs. This interfacial treatment increases the density of surface hydroxyl species and enables hierarchical multipoint interfacial anchoring dominated by metal-oxygen coordination, with Cl- induced hydrogen-bonding interactions acting cooperatively, thereby enhancing anchoring robustness and improving tolerance to thermo-mechanical stress accumulation. With this interfacial strategy, the devices achieve a power conversion efficiency of 27.3% (26.9% certified) and retain 94% of their initial efficiency after 400 temperature cycles between -40 and 85 degrees C (ISOS-T-3). These results demonstrate that rational regulation of buried interfacial anchoring architectures can simultaneously enhance device efficiency and long-term operational reliability, offering a viable pathway toward high-efficiency and durable perovskite photovoltaics.

infographic.key_insight: Hierarchical multipoint anchoring strengthens buried interfaces in inverted perovskite solar cells, improving efficiency and resistance to thermal cycling.
infographic.engineering_relevance: Engineering interfacial adhesion offers a route to reduce stress-driven device failure under realistic temperature fluctuations.
method: Pretreat transparent conductive oxides with a homometallic halide to guide ordered self-assembled monolayer formation.
Increase surface hydroxyl density to strengthen metal–oxygen coordination.
Use cooperative chloride-induced hydrogen bonding to reinforce interfacial anchoring.
infographic.evidence_signal: Devices achieved 27.3% efficiency (26.9% certified) and retained 94% of initial efficiency after 400 ISOS-T-3 temperature cycles between −40 and 85 °C.
infographic.watch_item: Thermal-cycle durability does not alone establish long-term field reliability or compatibility with large-area manufacturing.
infographic.paper_title: Hierarchical interfacial anchoring for durable perovskite solar cells

title: Dynamic Molecular Transformation Mediated Crystallization Regulation and Interface Passivation in Tin Based Perovskite Solar Cells
authors: Ying Tang, Zuhong Zhang, Hongzhuo Wu, Zhihao Li, Zhenhuang Su, Yonggang Yang
abstract: Tin-based perovskites are promising candidates for lead-free photovoltaics but suffer from labile Sn$^{2+}$ coordination, rapid crystallization, and severe interfacial defects. Here, we develop a dynamic molecular transformation using 1-acetylpiperazine (PX) to regulate crystallization and interface chemistry simultaneously. During nucleation and growth, the carbonyl group coordinates with Sn$^{2+}$ to stabilize precursor complexes, moderate supersaturation, and enable controlled crystal growth. Upon annealing, PX undergoes in situ molecular transformation, suggested to form amidinium-functionalized species that preferentially occupy surface A-site vacancies, forming a passivation layer and suppressing nonradiative recombination. This coupled bulk-to-interface evolution yields compact, highly crystalline films with improved optoelectronic quality. Devices achieve a power conversion efficiency of 15.18% and retain 94.1% of initial efficiency after 500 h of continuous illumination. This work demonstrates a dynamic molecular engineering approach integrating crystallization control and interface passivation, providing a pathway toward efficient and stable lead-free perovskite photovoltaics.

infographic.key_insight: 1-acetylpiperazine (PX) couples crystallization control with interface passivation to improve lead-free tin-based perovskite solar cells.
infographic.engineering_relevance: A dynamically transforming additive offers a route to improving film quality and operational stability within the same fabrication process.
method: Coordinate PX carbonyl groups with Sn²⁺ to stabilize precursor complexes and regulate crystal growth.
Anneal films to induce PX transformation, suggested to produce amidinium-functionalized species.
Passivate surface A-site vacancies to suppress nonradiative recombination.
infographic.evidence_signal: The abstract reports 15.18% power conversion efficiency and retention of 94.1% of initial efficiency after 500 hours of continuous illumination.
infographic.watch_item: The proposed amidinium-forming transformation remains tentative, and the abstract does not specify illumination-test conditions or device statistics.
infographic.paper_title: Dynamic Molecular Transformation Mediated Crystallization Regulation and Interface Passivation in Tin Based Perovskite Solar Cells

title: Strain-Induced Tetragonal-to-Cubic Transition in MAPbI$_3$ from Machine-Learned Molecular Dynamics
authors: Daan Holleman, Luuk Klein Nagelvoort, Monica Morales-Masis, Linn Leppert
abstract: Metal-halide perovskites are promising photovoltaic absorbers whose optoelectronic properties are highly tunable. Epitaxial strain offers a route to stabilize desirable phases, tune band gaps, and reduce energetic disorder, but rational strain engineering requires predictive models. Static, zero-temperature "strained-bulk" density functional theory (DFT) calculations, successful for oxide perovskites, neglect the dynamic disorder and anharmonicity that govern halide perovskites at ambient temperature. Here, we show that molecular dynamics (MD) based on machine-learned force fields trained on-the-fly on DFT reproduces the structural and optoelectronic response of methylammonium (MA) lead iodide (MAPbI$_3$) to epitaxial strain at 300 K. We simulate bulk and free-standing slab models across experimentally accessible biaxial strains by locking the in-plane lattice vectors in nanosecond-long simulations. We predict a tetragonal-to-cubic transition at $\sim$0.5% tensile strain, marked by $c/a = 1$ and the loss of the $a^0a^0c^-$ tilting pattern, in agreement with experiments on epitaxial MAPbI$_3$ films on KCl. MA cations retain preferential orientations in the strain-induced cubic phase, unlike in its temperature-induced counterpart. Bulk and slab models yield consistent trends, with surface effects decaying within a few octahedral layers. Band gaps computed as ensemble averages over MD snapshots blue-shift under tensile strain, consistent with experiment, whereas static calculations on averaged structures predict a red shift. Our study positions MD with constrained lattice vectors as a method for predicting finite-temperature strain phase diagrams and guiding the epitaxial design of perovskite absorbers.

infographic.key_insight: Machine-learned molecular dynamics predicts that about 0.5% biaxial tensile strain drives MAPbI₃ from tetragonal to cubic at 300 K while blue-shifting its band gap.
infographic.engineering_relevance: Finite-temperature strain modeling can guide epitaxial design of perovskite solar absorbers where static calculations miss dynamic structural and optical responses.
method: Train machine-learned force fields on-the-fly using DFT.
Run nanosecond bulk and free-standing slab simulations with fixed in-plane lattice vectors.
Track structural changes and average band gaps over MD snapshots.
infographic.evidence_signal: The predicted transition agrees with experiments on MAPbI₃ films on KCl, bulk and slab trends are consistent, and ensemble band gaps reproduce the experimental tensile-strain blue shift.
infographic.watch_item: Free-standing slabs do not explicitly capture substrate interfaces, so interface-specific effects remain an implementation concern.
infographic.paper_title: Strain-Induced Tetragonal-to-Cubic Transition in MAPbI$_3$ from Machine-Learned Molecular Dynamics

title: Interpretable machine learning diagnosis of degradation mechanisms in lead-free $RbSn_{0.5}Ge_{0.5}I_{3}$ solar cells from temperature- and illumination-dependent electrical measurements
authors: Nabanita Sarker, Hafiz Imtiaz
abstract: Machine learning coupled with device simulation is widely used to optimize thin-film solar cells, but almost exclusively in the forward direction, from device parameters to predicted performance. The inverse problem encountered after fabrication, namely identifying the mechanism that limits a given device, is still addressed by manual inspection of characterization data. In this work, both directions are examined for lead-free $RbSn_{0.5}Ge_{0.5}I_{3}$ solar cells using approximately 42,000 SCAPS-1D simulations. Replacing the Spiro-OMeTAD hole transport layer with CuI increases the simulated power conversion efficiency from 19.6\% to 21.6\%, almost entirely through the fill factor. Surrogate models trained and tested on a factorial parameter grid substantially overstate their predictive accuracy. An XGBoost regressor attains $R^2 = 0.9997$ on held-out grid points but only 0.58 on independently sampled devices, whereas training on a Latin hypercube design of comparable size restores $R^2 = 0.995$. For the inverse problem, a multi-label classifier identifies which of six degradation mechanisms are present from simulated temperature- and illumination-dependent open-circuit-voltage measurements. It achieves a macro $F_1$ score of 0.938, compared to 0.687 for a calibrated physics-rule baseline. The classifier does not, however, generalize to combinations of mechanisms absent from the training set.

infographic.key_insight: Machine learning can diagnose simulated degradation mechanisms in lead-free solar cells from electrical measurements, but apparent accuracy depends strongly on training-data design.
infographic.engineering_relevance: The approach could support post-fabrication fault diagnosis, while simulations suggest replacing Spiro-OMeTAD with CuI raises efficiency from 19.6% to 21.6%, mainly through fill-factor gains.
method: Run approximately 42,000 SCAPS-1D simulations of RbSn0.5Ge0.5I3 solar cells.
Compare forward-prediction surrogates trained on factorial grids versus Latin hypercube samples.
Use a multi-label classifier to identify six degradation mechanisms from temperature- and illumination-dependent open-circuit voltage.
infographic.evidence_signal: On simulated data, diagnosis achieved macro F1 = 0.938 versus 0.687 for a calibrated physics-rule baseline; forward-prediction R² fell from 0.9997 on held-out grid points to 0.58 on independently sampled devices, but reached 0.995 with Latin hypercube training.

infographic.paper_title: Interpretable machine learning diagnosis of degradation mechanisms in lead-free $RbSn_{0.5}Ge_{0.5}I_{3}$ solar cells from temperature- and illumination-dependent electrical measurements

title: Persistent Neutron Irradiation Effects and Partial Recovery in Thin-Film CdS/CdTe Solar Cells
authors: Ashraful Mamun, Andrew Allison, Meng-Jen, Wang, Etee Kawna Roy, Edward Cazalas
abstract: Thin-film CdTe solar cells are promising candidates for lightweight space power, but device-level studies of their response to neutron irradiation remain scarce. Here, we report the device performance of CdS/CdTe solar cells irradiated for 10 to 150 min in the thermal irradiator of a TRIGA reactor (90 kW), corresponding to nominal total neutron fluences of 3.3 x 10^14 to 5.0 x 10^15 n cm-2. The cells were characterized after 18 months of post-irradiation storage, once the residual activity has decayed to background levels. Co-irradiated FTO-coated glass reference substrates exhibit a wavelength-dependent transmission loss, with the transmittance at 500 nm decreasing from 80 % to 50 % after 60 min of irradiation. The irradiated cells retain rectifying behavior, but the reverse-bias dark current, photocurrent, and efficiency generally decrease with exposure time. Post-irradiation annealing at 70 °C under one-sun illumination initially improves Jsc and Voc, with the highest efficiency after 4 h. Prolonged annealing, however, causes substantial FF degradation despite continued photocurrent recovery. These trends suggest that irradiation-induced changes in the glass substrate, CdTe absorber, and contacts respond differently to annealing. Understanding underlying defect chemistry and correlating it with device behavior are necessary steps toward radiation-tolerant CdTe photovoltaics for space applications.

infographic.key_insight: CdS/CdTe solar cells show persistent performance losses after neutron irradiation, while mild light-assisted annealing provides only partial recovery.
infographic.engineering_relevance: Space-power designs using thin-film CdTe must account for radiation damage across the substrate, absorber, and contacts, as well as trade-offs during annealing.
method: Irradiated cells in a 90 kW TRIGA reactor for 10–150 min at nominal neutron fluences of 3.3 × 10^14–5.0 × 10^15 n cm⁻².
Characterized devices after 18 months of storage and measured transmission through co-irradiated FTO-coated glass.
Evaluated post-irradiation annealing at 70 °C under one-sun illumination.

infographic.watch_item: Delayed characterization and unresolved defect mechanisms limit predictions of in-orbit degradation and optimal recovery protocols.
infographic.paper_title: Persistent Neutron Irradiation Effects and Partial Recovery in Thin-Film CdS/CdTe Solar Cells

title: Effects of Yttrium doping on Proton Conductivity in Ba(Fe, Co, Zr, Y)O$_{3-δ}$ Cathode Materials for Proton Ceramic Fuel Cells
authors: Chiyoung Kim, Ryan Jacobs, Jun Meng, Jack H. Duffy, Kyle S. Brinkman, Yueh-Lin Lee
abstract: Protonic ceramic fuel cells (PCFCs) offer efficient energy conversion at intermediate temperatures, but their performance is often constrained by sluggish oxygen reduction kinetics at the cathode. Triple conducting perovskite materials such as BaCo$_x$Fe$_y$Zr$_z$Y$_{1-x-y-z}$O$_{3-δ}$ (BCFZY) have shown promise as air electrodes. In this study, we investigated the impact of Y doping on proton conductivity by decoupling the effects on proton diffusivity and proton concentration. Using ab initio molecular dynamics (AIMD) simulations, we assessed proton tracer diffusivity across three compositions: BaCo$_{0.4}$Fe$_{0.4}$Zr$_{0.2}$O$_{3-δ}$ (BCFZ), BaCo$_{0.4}$Fe$_{0.4}$Zr$_{0.1}$Y$_{0.1}$O$_{3-δ}$ (BCFZY0.1) and BaCo$_{0.4}$Fe$_{0.4}$Y$_{0.2}$O$_{3-δ}$ (BCFY). Thermodynamic defect models incorporating hydration, oxidation, and hydride formation reactions are employed to estimate temperature-dependent proton concentrations. Our results suggest that increasing the Y content from BCFZ to BCFY increases proton diffusivity by 1.7% at 500 $^\circ$C. Under PCFC operating gas conditions, proton concentration and proton conductivity are predicted to increase by 3.8% and 5.3%, respectively, at 500 $^\circ$C. These increases are modest compared with the larger enhancements reported experimentally under reducing conditions, highlighting the importance of gas conditions in evaluating the effects of Y doping. Under low oxygen partial pressure conditions, we predict that the dominant proton transport mechanism shifts from hydroxyl groups (OH$_O^{\bullet}$) to hydride species (H$_O^{\bullet}$). This work provides mechanistic insight into proton transport in BCFZY cathodes and offers design principles for optimizing proton-conducting air electrodes in next-generation PCFCs.

infographic.key_insight: Increasing Y substitution in BCFZY perovskite cathodes modestly improves predicted proton transport at 500 °C, with gas conditions strongly influencing the transport mechanism.
infographic.engineering_relevance: The findings guide protonic ceramic fuel cell cathode design—not solar cells—by linking Y content and operating atmosphere to proton conductivity.
method: Compare BCFZ, BCFZY0.1, and BCFY compositions.
Use ab initio molecular dynamics to estimate proton tracer diffusivity.
Model hydration, oxidation, and hydride formation to predict proton concentrations.
infographic.evidence_signal: From BCFZ to BCFY at 500 °C, calculations predict 1.7% higher proton diffusivity and, under PCFC operating gases, 3.8% higher proton concentration and 5.3% higher proton conductivity.
infographic.watch_item: The predicted gains depend on gas conditions; larger experimental enhancements under reducing conditions may involve a shift from hydroxyl-mediated to hydride-mediated transport.
infographic.paper_title: Effects of Yttrium doping on Proton Conductivity in Ba(Fe, Co, Zr, Y)O$_{3-δ}$ Cathode Materials for Proton Ceramic Fuel Cells

title: DeepDOSReasoner: Physics-Grounded Reasoning for Density-of-States Prediction and Materials Discovery
authors: Yingheng Wang, Francesco Ricci, Zhilong Wang, Tao Yu, Junwen Bai, Xiangyun Lei
abstract: Predicting a material's behavior from its atomic structure is a longstanding goal of the physical sciences. The electronic and phonon densities of states (eDOS and phDOS) govern key electronic, optical, vibrational, and thermodynamic properties, yet their calculation using density functional theory (DFT) is costly: about 60% of Materials Project entries lack eDOS and over 80% lack phDOS. Existing crystal-to-spectrum models rely on pooled structural representations and pointwise regression, which blur spectral features and violate total-state conservation. Here we introduce DeepDOSReasoner, a physics-grounded framework that decodes spectra through atom-to-energy source attention and refines the normalized DOS through learned continuity-equation transport, enforcing nonnegativity and total-state conservation by construction. DeepDOSReasoner achieves the highest prediction accuracy across all evaluated metrics for both eDOS and phDOS, recovers element-resolved contributions without supervision, and most reliably identifies rare valence-band (VB) gaps. In a prospective screen of 8,106 uncharted materials validated by new DFT calculations, its predictions remain the most accurate among the methods evaluated, with 25 of its top 50 candidates confirmed as VB-gap materials. Three case studies spanning substituted compounds, photovoltaic chalcogenides, and a high-entropy alloy demonstrate transfer across materials classes. Ablations confirm that both stages are necessary, while the model retains comparable accuracy when trained on only 25% of the data. Predicting spectra in milliseconds enables exhaustive screening; we release predictions filling the missing eDOS for 91,405 and phDOS for 127,768 Materials Project entries. DeepDOSReasoner provides a blueprint for integrating machine learning with physical reasoning toward high-throughput spectral screening and autonomous materials discovery.

infographic.key_insight: DeepDOSReasoner predicts electronic and phonon density-of-states spectra from crystal structures while enforcing nonnegativity and total-state conservation.
infographic.engineering_relevance: Millisecond spectral predictions could accelerate materials screening, including photovoltaic chalcogenides, but do not directly establish solar-cell efficiency.
method: Map atomic structure to spectra with atom-to-energy source attention.
Refine normalized spectra using learned continuity-equation transport.
Screen candidate materials for rare valence-band gaps.
infographic.evidence_signal: The abstract reports the best accuracy among evaluated methods for both spectrum types and new DFT validation of an 8,106-material screen, confirming valence-band gaps in 25 of the top 50 candidates.
infographic.watch_item: DFT-validated spectral predictions still require experimental and device-level validation before use in solar-cell design.
infographic.paper_title: DeepDOSReasoner: Physics-Grounded Reasoning for Density-of-States Prediction and Materials Discovery

title: AgBiS2 near-infrared absorbers for thin film tandem photovoltaics
authors: Shiling Dong, Yongjie Wang, Hae-Jun Seok, Mengyuan Huang, Edward Newton, Der Ying Chen
abstract: AgBiS2 has rapidly risen in efficiency as single-junction photovoltaics (PVs), but its potential for tandem PVs is unexplored. Herein, we perform optical modeling based on the experimental absorption spectrum of AgBiS2, revealing that, as the NIR sub-cell, efficiencies exceeding 47.5% are achievable in triple-junction tandems, superseding tandems using Pb/Sn perovskite NIR cells (44.2%). However, fulfilling this potential requires overcoming the limited transport properties of AgBiS2 nanocrystal films, which constrains film thicknesses to only 30-50 nm, severely restricting NIR response. A solution-phase ligand exchange process is herein developed, allowing one-step deposition of passivated AgBiS2 nanocrystals that maintain efficient charge-carrier extraction despite an order of magnitude increase in film thickness. These films enable 24.0%-efficient four-terminal tandems with visible-light-absorbing lead-halide perovskite sub-cells, and monolithic tandems successfully demonstrating voltage addition. AgBiS2 PVs have high stability, retaining >90% of the original efficiency after 3 months of storage in dry air without encapsulation. This work establishes the significant potential of AgBiS2 as a stable and scalable NIR absorber for tandem PVs.

infographic.key_insight: Solution-phase ligand exchange enables thicker AgBiS2 near-infrared absorbers with efficient charge extraction, supporting 24.0%-efficient four-terminal perovskite tandems.
infographic.engineering_relevance: One-step deposition of passivated AgBiS2 nanocrystals offers a route toward scalable near-infrared sub-cells for thin-film tandem photovoltaics.
method: Model tandem performance using the experimental AgBiS2 absorption spectrum.
Use solution-phase ligand exchange to enable an order-of-magnitude increase in absorber thickness.
Integrate AgBiS2 with visible-light-absorbing perovskites in four-terminal and monolithic tandems.
infographic.evidence_signal: The abstract reports 24.0% four-terminal tandem efficiency, voltage addition in monolithic tandems, and >90% efficiency retention after three months of unencapsulated dry-air storage; triple-junction efficiencies above 47.5% are modeled, not demonstrated.
infographic.watch_item: Dry-air storage stability does not establish operational durability under illumination, heat, or humidity.
infographic.paper_title: AgBiS2 near-infrared absorbers for thin film tandem photovoltaics

title: Lattice Thermal Conductivity of MgO and the MgSiO$_3$ Polymorphs Bridgmanite and Post-Perovskite at Lower-Mantle Conditions Using Fine-Tuned MACE Potentials
authors: Amrendra Kumar Tiwari, Sandro Jahn
abstract: Heat flow across the core-mantle boundary (CMB) depends on the lattice thermal conductivity ($κ_{\mathrm{latt}}$) of lowermost-mantle minerals, yet calculated CMB values for MgO differ severalfold, and high-temperature estimates of the conductivity increase across the bridgmanite-post-perovskite transition range from about 20 to 50%. Direct solutions of the linearized phonon Boltzmann transport equation (LBTE) require thousands of density functional theory (DFT) force evaluations per thermodynamic state. Here we replace these evaluations with phase-specific, fine-tuned MACE potentials for MgO, MgSiO3 bridgmanite (Pv), and MgSiO3 post-perovskite (PPv). The potentials reproduce DFT energies, forces, stresses, pressure-volume relations, and compressed-state phonons for all three phases. For MgO at 0 GPa, replacing MACE forces with DFT forces in otherwise identical transport calculations changes $κ_{\mathrm{latt}}$ by 0.2% at 300 K and 1.9% at 2000 K. PPv is 44-55% more conductive than Pv at the same pressure and temperature and strongly anisotropic, with $κ_{[100]}/κ_{[010]}$ ranging from 1.7 to 2.1. The quasi-harmonic phase boundary has a Clapeyron slope of $(7.4 \pm 0.1)$ MPa/K and intersects a model geotherm at 116.2 GPa and 2660 K, where the transition raises the silicate conductivity by 47%, to 8.6 W/(m K). Heating in the basal thermal boundary layer lowers the MgO and PPv conductivities to 37.3 and 6.7 W/(m K) at the CMB, where Hashin-Shtrikman bounds of 9.5-11.4 W/(m K) for an Fe-free aggregate of 80 vol% silicate and 20 vol% MgO encompass the 10 W/(m K) used in earlier heat-flow estimates. The density-temperature parameterizations provide an intrinsic end-member reference for lower-mantle thermal models.

infographic.key_insight: Fine-tuned MACE potentials predict that MgSiO₃ post-perovskite conducts 44–55% more lattice heat than bridgmanite at equal pressure and temperature.
infographic.engineering_relevance: This computational geoscience study—not solar-cell research—provides thermal-conductivity inputs for lower-mantle and core–mantle boundary heat-flow models.
method: Fine-tune phase-specific MACE potentials for MgO, bridgmanite, and post-perovskite.
Replace DFT force evaluations in linearized phonon Boltzmann transport calculations.
Combine phase-boundary calculations with aggregate conductivity bounds.
infographic.evidence_signal: For MgO at 0 GPa, replacing MACE forces with DFT forces changes predicted conductivity by only 0.2% at 300 K and 1.9% at 2000 K.
infographic.watch_item: The reported core–mantle boundary aggregate bounds of 9.5–11.4 W/(m K) assume an Fe-free mixture of 80 vol% silicate and 20 vol% MgO, limiting direct application to chemically complex mantle materials.
infographic.paper_title: Lattice Thermal Conductivity of MgO and the MgSiO$_3$ Polymorphs Bridgmanite and Post-Perovskite at Lower-Mantle Conditions Using Fine-Tuned MACE Potentials

title: Battery Energy Storage Sizing in PV Ramp-Rate Smoothing using Constraint-Aware Reinforcement Learning-Based Controller
authors: Arash Omidi, Tanmay Mishra, Mads R. Almassalkhi
abstract: This paper presents a constraint-aware reinforcement learning (CARL) controller for battery energy storage system (BESS) sizing and photovoltaic (PV) ramp-rate smoothing. Rapid PV power fluctuations caused by cloud transitions can introduce operational and stability challenges in power systems. To mitigate these impacts, grid codes impose ramp-rate limits (RRL) on PV power injected to the grid. BESSs can support such grid codes by absorbing or supplying power during rapid variations. However, the extent to which BESSs can reduce PV-induced variability depends on (i) the BESS power and energy capacities; and (ii) the adopted controller. Thus, BESS sizing and controller design are coupled. Conventional moving-average control can increase battery usage due to filter-induced lag, while ramp-rate control is reactive and does not account for the long-term impact of actions on battery state of charge and future ramp events. Optimization-based methods can reduce BESS requirements by anticipating future PV variations, but their performance depends on accurate PV forecasts. To address these limitations, the CARL controller learns a causal state-feedback policy from historical PV data without requiring forecasts during deployment. Ramp-rate, converter-power, and state-of-charge constraints are incorporated into a causal feasibility interval that guarantees feasible actions by definition. A full-horizon input-convex neural network (ICNN)-based optimization is developed as a noncausal benchmark for the minimum achievable BESS requirements. Evaluation using three real-world PV datasets shows that, at a 10\%/min ramp-rate limit, CARL reduces peak BESS power by 8.7--10.4\% and energy capacity by 47.5--62.6\% relative to conventional ramp-rate control while maintaining the grid-codes compliance.

infographic.key_insight: Constraint-aware reinforcement learning smooths PV output while reducing required battery power and energy capacity relative to conventional ramp-rate control.
infographic.engineering_relevance: Joint battery sizing and controller design can reduce storage requirements for grid-compliant PV integration; this work concerns system operation, not perovskite cell materials.
method: Learn a causal state-feedback policy from historical PV data without deployment-time forecasts.
Enforce ramp-rate, converter-power, and state-of-charge constraints through a causal feasibility interval.
Use full-horizon input-convex neural network optimization as a noncausal sizing benchmark.
infographic.evidence_signal: Across three real-world PV datasets at a 10%/min ramp-rate limit, CARL reduced peak battery power by 8.7–10.4% and energy capacity by 47.5–62.6% versus conventional ramp-rate control while maintaining grid-code compliance.
infographic.watch_item: Deployment should verify that the feasibility interval remains nonempty under extreme PV ramps and the selected battery power and energy limits.
infographic.paper_title: Battery Energy Storage Sizing in PV Ramp-Rate Smoothing using Constraint-Aware Reinforcement Learning-Based Controller

title: Inverse design of superconductors and semiconductors with differentiable foundation models
authors: Cristóbal Méndez, Justin Tahmassebpur, Tomás A. Arias
abstract: Designing a crystal for a target property requires choosing its elements, stoichiometry, and atomic structure together, yet gradients exist only for the continuous structural variables. We introduce differentiable Equiformer fast effective-atom theory (DEFEAT), which lets a pretrained EquiformerV3 foundation model accept continuous species weights and site occupancies without retraining on fractional data, thereby enabling gradient-based materials optimization. Gradients from fine-tuned property models and a machine-learned energy penalty then guide updates to composition, atom count, atomic positions, and lattice vectors in a single optimization. In a search for phonon-mediated superconductors, density-functional perturbation theory on 45 structurally novel designs gives isotropic Allen-Dynes critical temperatures above 10 K for 39; the highest is 24.0 K for ZrTiNb2CN3, and H4LiPd3 (23.2 K) lies on the static DFT hull. In searches for photovoltaic absorbers, SCAN calculations confirm ten novel crystal structures with band gaps within 20% of a 1.34 eV target on their respective raw or empirically corrected scales, all within 70 meV/atom of the DFT hull, and show that the systematic gap error of the training functional propagates into the designs unless the objective corrects for it. Quasiharmonic free energies from machine-learned potentials further show that finite-temperature competition with solid phases can reorder candidates relative to the static hull.

infographic.key_insight: Differentiable foundation models enable joint optimization of crystal composition and structure, yielding candidate photovoltaic absorbers near a target band gap.
infographic.engineering_relevance: This approach could accelerate solar-absorber screening by optimizing electronic properties alongside an energy-based stability penalty.
method: Extend pretrained EquiformerV3 to continuous species weights and site occupancies without fractional-data retraining.
Use property-model gradients and a learned energy penalty to update composition, atom count, positions, and lattice vectors.
Validate absorber candidates with SCAN calculations and assess finite-temperature phase competition.
infographic.evidence_signal: SCAN calculations confirm ten novel absorber structures with gaps within 20% of 1.34 eV on their respective raw or empirically corrected scales, all within 70 meV/atom of the DFT hull.
infographic.watch_item: Training-functional band-gap bias propagates into designs unless corrected in the objective; these computational candidates are not demonstrated solar cells.
infographic.paper_title: Inverse design of superconductors and semiconductors with differentiable foundation models

title: Will national renewable costs continue declining?
authors: C. Lennart Baumgärtner, J. Doyne Farmer
abstract: Since the 1980s, the global average solar photovoltaic (PV) cost has decreased by about two orders of magnitude while the global average onshore wind cost has decreased by about one order of magnitude. But global averages are only part of the story: For both solar and wind, costs vary between countries by about an order of magnitude. We curate a comprehensive database of national costs and build predictive models for future costs by decomposing the levelized cost of electricity (LCOE) into its components at the national level and modeling them separately. For solar we find that since 1990 the module cost and the balance of system (BOS) cost have both declined roughly exponentially at rates of 12% per year. In contrast, wind turbine cost has declined roughly exponentially by 4% per year, while BOS cost has not declined at all. This suggests that total global wind cost will approach a floor cost of about 35 USD/MWh, reaching about 43 USD/MWh in 2050, whereas global solar cost will continue to decline exponentially, reaching about 8 USD/MWh in 2050. For solar, about half of the cross-sectional variations in national LCOE costs is due to variations in capacity factors, though capital costs also play an important role. For wind, the cross-sectional variations are split approximately equally between capacity factor, capital costs, and investment costs. National BOS costs revert to global costs with a timescale of about 5-7 years, while variations in other factors are more persistent. We develop a simple model for predicting the deviations from global costs and show that it makes reasonable predictions with predictable errors. Finally, we compare our predictions to recent projections of integrated assessment models, and show that China has only accounted for about 0.05% of the overall decline in solar energy costs.

infographic.key_insight: The models project global solar PV costs falling to about 8 USD/MWh by 2050, while onshore wind reaches about 43 USD/MWh and approaches a 35 USD/MWh floor.
infographic.engineering_relevance: National renewable-energy planning should account for technology-specific cost trends, local capacity factors, capital costs, and financing conditions rather than relying solely on global averages.
method: Curate a comprehensive database of national solar PV and onshore wind costs.
Decompose national levelized electricity costs and model each component separately.
Predict national deviations from global costs and compare forecasts with integrated assessment model projections.
infographic.evidence_signal: Historical analysis finds solar module and balance-of-system costs declining roughly 12% annually since 1990, versus 4% for wind turbines and no decline in wind balance-of-system costs.
infographic.watch_item: The 2050 estimates depend on modeled cost trends; this is renewable-cost forecasting research, not an AI-driven solar-cell design study.
infographic.paper_title: Will national renewable costs continue declining?

title: Spin-vibronic order in Ba$_2$MgReO$_6$
authors: Zhishuo Huang, Takumi Gengo, Teruki Matsuzaki, Liviu F. Chibotaru, Naoya Iwahara
abstract: Strong spin-orbit coupling in $5d$ ions produces multipolar orders that conventional probes barely detect. In cubic $5d^1$ double perovskites, the spin-orbit quartet couples to Jahn-Teller vibrations, and resonant inelastic x-ray scattering (RIXS) has established the resulting spin-orbit-lattice entangled (vibronic) states [Phys. Rev. Lett. \textbf{133}, 036501 (2024)]. We proposed that these vibronic states order cooperatively and thereby explain the hidden quadrupole and canted magnetic phases of Ba$_2$MgReO$_6$ [Phys. Rev. B \textbf{107}, L220404 (2023)], but that proposal rested on a simplified model. Here, we show that a spin-vibronic Hamiltonian derived from first principles, with a single scale factor for the elastic coupling, reproduces the ordered phases of Ba$_2$MgReO$_6$ with the same vibronic states that describe its RIXS spectra. With this factor bringing the quadrupolar transition to 34.7 K, near the measured 33 K, the theory predicts the magnetic transition at 19.3 K, against the measured 18 K, and reproduces the antiferro distortion and the ferro elongation between the transitions. These results support spin-vibronic order in Ba$_2$MgReO$_6$ and point to it as the origin of the hidden multipolar phases of $5d^1$ double perovskites.

infographic.key_insight: A first-principles spin-vibronic model explains the hidden quadrupolar and canted magnetic phases of Ba₂MgReO₆ through cooperative ordering of coupled electronic and vibrational states.
infographic.engineering_relevance: The work informs modeling of spin–orbit-coupled quantum materials, rather than AI or perovskite solar-cell engineering.
method: Derive a spin-vibronic Hamiltonian from first principles.
Use the vibronic states that describe RIXS spectra.
Adjust one elastic-coupling scale factor to set the quadrupolar transition temperature.
infographic.evidence_signal: The model gives quadrupolar and magnetic transitions at 34.7 K and 19.3 K, versus measured values of 33 K and 18 K, and reproduces antiferro distortion and ferro elongation between transitions.
infographic.watch_item: One elastic-coupling scale factor is calibrated; applicability beyond Ba₂MgReO₆ remains to be established.
infographic.paper_title: Spin-vibronic order in Ba$_2$MgReO$_6$

title: Periodic Trends in Oxygen Vacancy Formation Energies Across Binary Main-Group Metal Oxides
authors: Manish Kumar, Bridget S. Ferris, Avital Isakov, Robert B. Wexler
abstract: The function of oxide materials, from solid-oxide fuel cells to solar thermochemical fuel production, depends on their oxygen vacancies. Their formation energetics have been mapped systematically for ternary perovskites, but reported values for the binary oxides, their conceptual and thermochemical building blocks, remain scattered across studies with differing computational methods. Here we report a systematic r$^2$SCAN density functional theory survey of neutral oxygen vacancy formation energies across 39 binary main-group metal oxide polymorphs spanning groups 1, 2, 13, 14, and 15, using the ShakeNBreak method to locate reconstructed defect ground states. The formation energies span 8 eV and decrease down each group and, for most multivalent cations, with increasing oxidation state. Both trends follow the reducibility of the cation. An interpretable crystal feature model is fit to these energies; its inputs are properties of the pristine bulk, with the reduction potential alternatively taken from tabulated thermochemistry. Retaining only its two dominant descriptors, the crystal reduction potential and the band gap, the model reproduces the formation energies with a held-out mean absolute error of 0.31 eV, lower than that of its four-descriptor parent model for transition-metal perovskites. The bond-breaking and stability terms of the full Born-Haber fit prove statistically null for the binary oxides, and the largest residuals identify the hosts where electron accommodation departs from the cation-reduction picture that the descriptors encode. The dataset provides a benchmark for machine-learning interatomic potentials, and the model estimates vacancy formation energies of main-group oxides from bulk properties alone.

infographic.key_insight: Neutral oxygen vacancy formation energies in binary main-group oxides are largely captured by two bulk descriptors: crystal reduction potential and band gap.
infographic.engineering_relevance: The model can help screen oxide materials for vacancy-dependent energy applications without explicit defect calculations, though solar-cell performance was not evaluated.
method: Surveyed 39 binary oxide polymorphs using r²SCAN density functional theory.
Used ShakeNBreak to identify reconstructed defect ground states.
Fit an interpretable model using pristine-bulk properties.
infographic.evidence_signal: Formation energies spanned 8 eV, and the two-descriptor model achieved a held-out mean absolute error of 0.31 eV.
infographic.watch_item: Predictions require caution when vacancy electrons are accommodated through mechanisms other than cation reduction.
infographic.paper_title: Periodic Trends in Oxygen Vacancy Formation Energies Across Binary Main-Group Metal Oxides

title: Analytical Framework Relating Capacitance-Frequency Measurements and Hysteresis in Perovskite Solar Cells
authors: Manjeet Kumar, Changzeng Ding, Mathias Nyman, Yongqi Sun, Chang-Qi Ma, Ronald Österbacka
abstract: Mobile ion migration strongly influences the electrical response and current-voltage hysteresis of perovskite solar cells. However, quantitative determination of ionic transport parameters typically requires transient measurements, extensive numerical simulations, and/or fitting procedures involving multiple uncertain parameters. Here, we present an analytical model that establishes a direct relationship between capacitance-frequency (C-f) characteristics and ionic transport properties in perovskite solar cells, while accounting for interlayer effects. The model describes the transition from the ion-screened depletion capacitance at low frequencies to the geometric capacitance at high frequencies and demonstrates that the characteristic transition frequency provides a direct measure of the dielectric relaxation time for ions. Furthermore, the model establishes a quantitative connection between C-f characteristics and scan-rate-dependent current-voltage hysteresis, enabling prediction of the scan-rate window in which maximum hysteresis occurs. Drift-diffusion simulations show excellent agreement with the analytical predictions over wide ranges of ion density, ion mobility, transport-layer mobility and doping concentration. Experimental measurements confirm the predicted correlation between capacitance and hysteresis. By providing a direct, physically transparent, and computationally efficient route for extracting ionic transport parameters from routine impedance measurements, this work offers a practical tool for quantifying ion migration and understanding dynamic phenomena in perovskite solar cells.

infographic.key_insight: An analytical model links capacitance–frequency measurements to ionic relaxation and predicts the scan-rate window of maximum current–voltage hysteresis in perovskite solar cells.
infographic.engineering_relevance: Routine impedance measurements could provide a computationally efficient route to estimating ionic transport properties and interpreting device hysteresis.
method: Model the transition from low-frequency ion-screened depletion capacitance to high-frequency geometric capacitance, including interlayer effects.
Relate the characteristic transition frequency to the ionic dielectric relaxation time.
Connect capacitance–frequency behavior to scan-rate-dependent current–voltage hysteresis.
infographic.evidence_signal: The abstract reports excellent agreement with drift–diffusion simulations across varied ionic and transport-layer parameters, plus experimental confirmation of the capacitance–hysteresis correlation.
infographic.watch_item: Parameter extraction requires accounting for interlayer effects; the abstract does not specify experimental uncertainty or the model’s full applicability limits.
infographic.paper_title: Analytical Framework Relating Capacitance-Frequency Measurements and Hysteresis in Perovskite Solar Cells

title: High-Entropy A-Site Disorder Enhances Oxygen Evolution Reaction Activity and Stability in Nickelate Thin Films
authors: Min-Ju Choi, Le Wang, Krishna Prasad Koirala, Hyoju Park, Mark E. Bowden, Elizabeth Helen Krenkel
abstract: Rare-earth nickelates are among the most active oxide electrocatalysts for the oxygen evolution reaction (OER), owing to their tunable Ni-O covalency, near-unity eg occupancy, and sensitivity to A-site chemistry, oxygen stoichiometry, and epitaxial strain. Here, we use epitaxial A-site high-entropy (La0.2Pr0.2Nd0.2Sm0.2Eu0.2)NiO3 thin films to reveal how epitaxial strain influences defect formation, Ni valence, electronic structure, and OER activity in a chemically disordered rare-earth (RE) sublattice. Tensile strain promotes Ruddlesden-Popper fault formation, interrupts the corner-sharing NiO6 network, and lowers the average Ni oxidation state. Although the occupied density of states near the Fermi level remains largely unchanged, O K-edge X-ray absorption spectroscopy reveals increased low-energy unoccupied states under tensile strain. First-principles calculations suggest that tensile strain shifts RE 4f-derived states toward the Fermi level, enhancing RE 4f-O 2p-Ni 3d hybridization. These coupled structural and electronic changes lead to earlier OER onset, stronger pre-catalytic Ni redox features, and higher activity than compressively strained films and representative single-A-site nickelates. The high-entropy nickelate also shows enhanced resistance to OER-induced structural degradation compared with LaNiO3. These results suggest that A-site configurational disorder and epitaxial strain can jointly tune defect formation and rare-earth-derived electronic states, providing a route for improving perovskite oxide electrocatalysts.

infographic.key_insight: A-site high-entropy disorder and tensile strain jointly enhance oxygen evolution activity in nickelate thin films, with improved structural stability relative to LaNiO3.
infographic.engineering_relevance: This research informs perovskite oxide electrocatalyst design for water splitting, rather than AI or solar-cell engineering.
method: Study epitaxial (La0.2Pr0.2Nd0.2Sm0.2Eu0.2)NiO3 films under different strain conditions.
Characterize defects, Ni valence, electronic structure, and OER performance.
Use first-principles calculations to interpret strain-dependent orbital hybridization.
infographic.evidence_signal: Tensile-strained films show earlier OER onset and higher activity than compressively strained films and representative single-A-site nickelates, while the high-entropy nickelate resists structural degradation better than LaNiO3.
infographic.watch_item: The abstract provides no quantitative activity or durability metrics, and scalability beyond epitaxial thin films remains unestablished.
infographic.paper_title: High-Entropy A-Site Disorder Enhances Oxygen Evolution Reaction Activity and Stability in Nickelate Thin Films

title: The Utility of Physics-Informed Machine Learning in Solar Power Production Forecasting
authors: Peter Pavlík, Franz M. Rohrhofer, Bernhard C. Geiger
abstract: Physics-informed machine learning (PIML) and hybrid modeling have attracted significant attention as approaches for combining physical knowledge with the flexibility of deep learning. In this work, we investigate whether these approaches deliver their commonly claimed benefits for large-scale photovoltaic (PV) power forecasting. We develop two hybrid forecasting architectures that integrate the ADR physical PV efficiency model with the TSMixer neural forecasting architecture through feature augmentation and residual learning. The proposed models are evaluated on a dataset comprising over 3 million samples from 3,713 PV installations across 33 European countries. We assess convergence speed, forecasting accuracy, transferability across geographical regions, and data efficiency. Although the physics-informed models seem to exhibit slightly faster convergence during training, they do not achieve consistent improvements in test-set accuracy, generalization, or performance under limited training data compared to the purely data-driven baseline. These findings suggest that, for modern deep forecasting architectures trained on large datasets, explicitly incorporating the ADR physical model provides limited practical benefit for day-ahead PV forecasting.

infographic.key_insight: Adding the ADR physical PV efficiency model to TSMixer offers limited practical benefit for day-ahead solar power forecasting compared with a purely data-driven baseline.
infographic.engineering_relevance: For large-scale PV forecasting, physics integration may add complexity without reliably improving accuracy, geographic transferability, or data efficiency.
method: Combine the ADR physical model with TSMixer through feature augmentation.
Build a second hybrid architecture using residual learning.
Compare hybrids with the data-driven baseline across training convergence, accuracy, geographic transfer, and limited-data performance.
infographic.evidence_signal: Evaluation used over 3 million samples from 3,713 PV installations across 33 European countries, finding slightly faster apparent convergence but no consistent gains in test accuracy, generalization, or limited-data performance.
infographic.watch_item: These findings concern ADR–TSMixer hybrids for day-ahead forecasting and should not be generalized to all physics-informed models or solar-cell design tasks.
infographic.paper_title: The Utility of Physics-Informed Machine Learning in Solar Power Production Forecasting
